checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: Medicine half: ch 18 delivers the redbark to Ranu. Nimmi doses eighteen courses for forty-one sick, and ch 20 shows Kiran's fever breaking. Ch 24 adds the masked buyer's sack, enough to finish the remaining twenty-three. Arrest half: ch 32 has Rohan tell the wardens before the meltwater runs, 'I am not arresting her. I am walking to Taravan beside her, with the law in her hand.' Gopal enters it in the post book. Two questions stay open, and both are tied to the hinge rather than left dangling. The first is the queen's final judgement, and ch 31 makes clear the Closing Roll bought peace for the crew, not a pardon for Meera. The second is the Old Bargain.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: Every non-series clue pays off on the page. C01, C04, C05, C07, C09, C13 and C15 pay off in ch 16, where the two leads build the Varun case from scraped lids, the gully route, the iron ring before the crack, the sieve mark, Lalit's 'three wardens', the fallback cut and the hunter's packet. C02 pays off in ch 22 with Kiran's account of the ear. C03 is recalled in ch 25 (the frozen skin in the warden report) and resolved in ch 29. C08 and C16 pay off in ch 29 with the cut end and the DIL badge. C10 pays off in ch 25, where Varun explains the lordship bounty for the stone. C11 is first noticed in ch 16 and paid off in ch 24, when Meera reties the cord in his double hitch with his slack. C20 pays off in ch 30 with 'Watch my hands' as a declaration, hands warm. C21 and C22 pay off in ch 28 (Asha's identification) and again in ch 30, where the clerk matches the two buttons. C23 pays off in ch 14, when Rohan burns a stick rather than answer about Puja's fine. C25 lands in two places: Jassi's small bell goes into Sunni's grave in ch 19, and ch 32 hangs Badami's big bell on the cairn and addresses Jassi. That is a deliberate split from the outline's single bell, and it still lands. C26 pays off in ch 27, with the torches circling the ash-marked houses until the grey-bearded officer stops them. No clue is orphaned. Continuity nit on C25: ch 31 describes Badami's big bell as worn 'through twelve winters of crossings', but ch 3 says Badami was too old for the run and her kid bell was the one Jassi carried. Worth a line edit.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: Ch 16 (midpoint chapter): 'I am the Salt Fox.' / 'My writ orders me to deliver the Salt Fox to the warden-judge at Taravan at the thaw.' Both leads stay warm-handed. They then deduce that Varun set the slide and is her middleman: 'My lifeline was your enemy's purse... I trusted the man who killed Jassi.' The first kiss follows, as does Rohan's binding promise, 'I will not let you fall on this mountain', which ties his body to her footing until the thaw. The romance shifts from guarded adversaries to complicit lovers who know exactly what divides them.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: Ch 1 belief: 'The law is only ever a noose for people like us.' She spits at the Closing Law and counts the empty peg on the hanging tree. Ch 30 choice: she writes 'Meera of Kothi Shilak, called the Salt Fox' into the crown's record and says, 'Law's a rope. Depends who ties it.' She then tells the assembly, 'I put it in the crown's record, under my own name, so that no one needs to guess.' Ch 31 confirms it when she takes the Closing Roll for life: 'I'll owe them winters. I'd give them anyway.' The chapter-1 Meera would never have entered her own name into the law's book or bound herself to it.

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: Ch 3: Jassi dies in the avalanche, is dug out dead with the bell in his fist, gets a cairn in ch 4, and is mourned through ch 32. Ch 18: Sunni, seven, dies before dawn after a dose given too late, and is buried in ch 19. Ch 26 and ch 31: Meera's left ring and little fingers die from the great lie and are amputated by Nimmi. None of these losses is reversed.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: Rohan's own mission is to carry the queen's lapis seal to the Snow Fair within twenty days, press it before the assembly and block Pritam's investiture (ch 2, ch 11, ch 30). Ch 21 adds a second goal: protecting his sister Ila, who is held at Garh Neshar. A third runs from ch 2 to ch 29: finding the smuggler on Dilan's rope. None of these depends on Meera.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: Ch 32: after the bond ends and they re-tie by choice, the cairn rings and the jogini speak through every palm: 'The bargain is owed... When the fourth winter ends, the pass closes. Forever. Unless someone pays.' The chapter then links the hinge to the carving's two unequal hands, to the grandfather's folded gloves, and to the queen wanting both Meera and Ila's map. It also plants Meera's fear that Kiran will try to pay the debt.

series_threads.thread: Carving of two hands on one rope. Ch 32 notes the hands are unequal (one broad, one long and narrow), which undercuts the 'two brothers in arms' chronicle and points to a warden and a smuggler making the Old Bargain.

Asha's three-loop knot matches the cairn carving. It reappears on the bound sentries in ch 28, where Asha silences Meera's question. This implies Asha's line has a connection to the original crossing.

Rohan's grandfather died on the pass the winter the Closing Law was written. Ch 32 adds that his gloves were found folded on a flat stone, which suggests a deliberate sacrifice tied to the Old Bargain.
The masked buyer pays in cut-corner Neshar silver and has access to the regent's stores. He refuses to give his name and is not identified in this book.
A grey-bearded officer lowers the torches at Ranu (ch 27) and lays down his sword belt at the Fair (ch 30). Nimmi learns his face, and his identity stays open.
The queen sealed the wax with her own blood. It proves the seal in ch 30 and leaves open what the queen knows of blood-bound magic and the Bargain.
The regent's general is officially exiled, but Ranu whispers otherwise (ch 31). This is likely the grey-bearded officer, and he may still be a power in the hills.

summary: The book meets every structural promise in novel-structure.md. Its central question is answered: the medicine reaches Ranu, and Rohan publicly refuses to arrest Meera at the thaw. Only the queen's judgement and the Old Bargain stay open, and both are explicitly bound to the series hinge. All nineteen non-series clues pay off on the page, most of them gathered into the ch 16 midpoint reveal. That reveal is a strong midpoint mirror: double confession, Varun exposed as both the saboteur and her supplier, then the first kiss under a binding promise. Meera's belief change is shown by a choice, not told: she enters her own name as the Salt Fox into the crown's record in ch 30 and takes the Closing Roll in ch 31. The losses are real and permanent: Jassi, Sunni and two of Meera's fingers. Rohan has independent goals in the seal, the coup and Ila. The ch 32 hinge resolves the bond and immediately opens the larger debt of the Old Bargain. The seven series threads are logged above. One minor continuity fix is suggested: ch 31's description of Badami's big bell as worn 'through twelve winters of crossings' sits awkwardly with ch 3, where Badami is too old for the run and Jassi carries her kid bell.
